tools.name: confirm_booking
tools.description: STEP 5, the committing call — turns a hold into a booking. payload = { hold_id } (from hold_slot). Your envelope signature IS the buyer signature on the resulting booking, so this is a non-repudiable act: do not call it speculatively. SIDE EFFECTS: returns { ok, status, booking_id, payment_status }

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "register_agent" references sensitive artifacts (private key, credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "register_agent" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_offers" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: register_agent · Private data: register_agent, list_offers · Public sink: register_agent, send_intent, hold_slot.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
